question: How can EOS decouple engineering intent and capability requirements from specific AI tool implementations (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor) using Hexagonal Ports & Adapters architecture?
scope: Tool-agnostic adapter patterns, Ports & Adapters architecture, capability routing, permission scoping, and synthetic mock tool validation
claims: Decoupling capability ports from vendor tool adapters prevents vendor lock-in and allows seamless tool substitution.
Capabilities should express intent and security boundaries, while adapters translate intent into vendor-specific tool calls.
evidence: Anthropic Model Context Protocol (MCP) demonstrates standard JSON-RPC schema translation across diverse tool providers.
Hexagonal Architecture (Ports & Adapters) in enterprise software isolates domain logic from infrastructure dependencies.
observations: Tool adapters must produce structured exit statuses, duration metrics, and verifiable EVD-*.json evidence payloads.
Fallback routing must never override security boundaries or external write barriers.
limitations: Adapters add an extra translation layer, requiring strict schema validation to avoid serialization latency.
recommendation: Adopt Hexagonal Ports & Adapters architecture for EOS Capability and Tool Registry.
